title: M2 PR #3 — Remediation of review feedback

decisions.ppx: ppx_deriving.eq + ppx_deriving.show; [@equal Yojson.Safe.equal] shim on Yojson fields; agent_message_equal kept by hand because synthetic = | (empty type) may confuse the deriver

stages.title: ppx_deriving across pera_types, pera_provider, pera_core
stages.description: Add ppx_deriving as a dependency and annotate all suitable types with [@deriving eq, show]. This eliminates the hand-written equality functions in agent_types.ml and adds pretty-printers to pera_types (addressing the 'helper for pretty printing Pera_types.Types values' comment). Types with Yojson.Safe.t fields get [@equal Yojson.Safe.equal] and [@printer ...] overrides.
implementation_notes: Add (depends (ppx_deriving (>= 1.6))) to dune-project. Add (preprocess (pps ppx_deriving.eq ppx_deriving.show)) to each affected dune library stanza.

pera_types/types.ml: add [@deriving eq, show] to: stop_reason, file_error_code, execution_error_code, tool_error, model, provenance, usage. For types containing Yojson.Safe.t (tool_call, tool_result_content, assistant_content, assistant_message, assistant_message_event), add [@deriving eq, show] with inline overrides: arguments: (Yojson.Safe.t [@equal Yojson.Safe.equal] [@printer (fun fmt v -> Format.pp_print_string fmt (Yojson.Safe.to_string v))]). user_content and user_message can be fully derived.

pera_provider/provider.ml: add [@deriving eq, show] to message (UserMessage / AssistantMessage / ToolResultMessage), context, tool_schema, simple_stream_options. These depend on pera_types equality which is now derived.

pera_core/agent_types.ml: add [@deriving eq, show] to tool_output, before_tool_call_result, turn_update. For agent_event, derive eq and show — each constructor field that contains agent_message or Yojson.Safe.t will need [@equal ...] overrides. For agent_message itself: Real contains Provider.message (now derived); Synthetic contains synthetic (= |, empty type) — keep agent_message_equal hand-written with | Real m1, Real m2 -> Provider.equal_message m1 m2 | Synthetic _, _ | _, Synthetic _ -> . since ppx_deriving may not handle empty variants cleanly.

Remove all hand-written equality functions from agent_types.ml that are now replaced by derived ones: stop_reason_equal, provenance_equal, usage_equal, assistant_content_equal, assistant_message_equal (keep only agent_message_equal as above), tool_result_content_equal. The agent_event_equal and assistant_message_event_equal can be replaced by the derived equal_agent_event and equal_assistant_message_event.

Update agent_types.mli: remove declarations for functions replaced by derived ones; keep agent_message_equal (still hand-written); pp_agent_event is now the derived show_agent_event or an alias — stage 3 will enhance it, so for now just expose the derived pp.
Update agent_event_testable to use the derived equal_agent_event.

existing_tests: All tests must remain green after the equality replacements — the derived eq must match the hand-written behaviour
test_requirements.test_command: dune build --root <worktree> && semgrep --config .semgrep/ --severity ERROR lib/ bin/ && dune runtest --root <worktree>

coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: type-safety.md — ppx attributes are type-safe; no loss of structural equality protection

stages.title: Refactor agent_loop.ml: flatten execute_one_tool and extract run_inner helpers
stages.description: Two readability fixes in agent_loop.ml: (1) flatten the nested option+result matching in execute_one_tool (comment on line 222) using let* or helper functions; (2) extract named helpers for the hook callbacks and tool-result collection in run_inner to reduce its length (comment on line 392).
implementation_notes: execute_one_tool (line 222): The current structure is match tool_opt with | None -> ... | Some tool -> (match validated_args_result with | Error -> ... | Ok () -> (match before_result with | Deny -> ... | Allow -> ...)). Refactor to use let* / Result monad or extract sub-steps as named local functions: let result_of_unknown_tool, let result_of_schema_error, let call_before_hook ~config ~final_agent_msg ~tc, let execute_and_emit. Each sub-step returns a (tool_result_content, [`Skip of tool_result_content]) to exit early. Alternatively, use a simple helper: let fail_tool ~tool_call_id ~tool_name ~msg out_stream = (push event; return result) and build the flow as a flat sequence of Result.bind calls.

run_inner (line 392): Extract the following as named helper functions: invoke_should_stop ~config ~final_agent_msg ~tool_results ~messages_ref (calls the hook, returns bool); invoke_prepare_next_turn ~config ~model_ref ~options_ref ~messages_ref ~final_agent_msg ~tool_results (calls the hook, mutates refs if update returned); inject_steering_messages ~config (calls get_steering_messages, returns list). The function should read top-to-bottom as a sequence of named steps.
No behaviour change — this is a pure readability refactor. All tests must pass unchanged.

stages.title: Http_client connection pool + Provider.S redesign
stages.description: Introduce Http_client.t wrapping a persistent Piaf.Client.t for connection reuse. Redesign Provider.S to have type t (provider instance) + create ~env ~sw, so that stream_simple takes the instance rather than ~env. Anthropic_provider.create ~env ~sw creates the Http_client and stores it; stream_simple reuses it across calls. Faux_provider.as_provider is updated to satisfy the new S (with unit as t). The stream_fn closure type in agent_types.mli is unchanged — callers bind the provider instance into the closure before passing it to the loop.
implementation_notes: http_client.mli changes: add 'type t' (abstract, wraps Piaf.Client.t); add 'val create : env:Eio_unix.Stdenv.base -> sw:Eio.Switch.t -> string -> (t, error) result' where the string is the base URL (e.g. 'https://api.anthropic.com'). Change post_stream signature from (~env ~sw ~headers ~body ~on_chunk url) to (~client:t ~headers ~body ~on_chunk path) where path is the request path appended to the base URL. The old one-shot function becomes an internal detail or is removed.

http_client.ml: implement create using Piaf.Client.create ~sw env (Uri.of_string base_url). The Piaf.Client.t is stored in the abstract type. post_stream uses Piaf.Client.call or Piaf.Client.post on the existing client. The client is tied to the switch passed to create — when the switch ends, the client is closed automatically (Piaf handles this via sw).

provider.mli changes: add 'type t' and 'val create : env:Eio_unix.Stdenv.base -> sw:Eio.Switch.t -> t' to module type S. Change stream_simple from (~env ~model ~context ~options ~sw) to (t -> ~model ~context ~options ~sw). The t is a first-class provider value holding the connection.

anthropic_provider.mli/ml: 'type t = { client: Http_client.t; api_key: string }'. create ~env ~sw reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env, calls Http_client.create, returns t. stream_simple (provider: t) ~model ~context ~options ~sw calls Http_client.post_stream ~client:provider.client.
faux_provider.ml: update as_provider to satisfy new Provider.S. type t = unit (stateless). create ~env:_ ~sw:_ = (). stream_simple () ~model ~context ~options ~sw = stream_fn_of_scripts scripts ...
provider_driver.ml: add let provider = Anthropic_provider.create ~env ~sw before the stream_simple call; update call site to Anthropic_provider.stream_simple provider ~model ~context ~options ~sw.
loop_driver.ml: the driver uses Faux_provider directly via stream_fn_of_scripts, not Provider.S, so minimal change is needed. Update as_provider usage if any.

http_client_test.ml: update test to use the new Http_client.create API. The test that drives post_stream against http://127.0.0.1:1/ must now call Http_client.create first (which will fail fast), asserting that create returns an Error with a non-empty error_to_string. Or: create succeeds (connection is lazy) and post_stream fails — either is acceptable, just verify error_to_string is non-empty.

existing_tests: All tests remain green; provider_driver still compiles and runs

new_tests.description: Call Http_client.create or Http_client.post_stream against an invalid URL and assert the returned Error has a non-empty error_to_string

test_requirements.test_command: dune build --root <worktree> && semgrep --config .semgrep/ --severity ERROR lib/ bin/ && dune runtest --root <worktree>

error-handling.md — create returns Result; never raises on connection failure
pera-specific.md §5 — ~sw labelled arg on create ties the client lifetime to the switch

summary: 6 stages; no epoch grouping needed. Stages 1, 4, 5, 6 are independent. Stage 2 depends on Stage 1 (uses derived pp functions in helpers). Stage 3 depends on Stage 1 (uses derived pp as base). Recommended order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 (linear, each PASS before next).
